newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan SEC urges brokers protect investor rights.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan SEC urges brokers protect investor rights.

text.p: Taiwan's Securities and Exchange Commission chief Lu Tung-ying sent a letter to the island's securities brokerages, urging them to protect investors' rights after recent market rallies, local newspapers said on Friday.
The letter urged brokers to protect investors' rights, secure brokerage shareholders' equity and perform their social responsibility, the papers said.
The Commercial Times newspaper quoted commission officials as saying the letter was a neutral one, hoping to caution brokers to strengthen their credit checking operations to avoid excess investment.
As of Thursday the index had risen some 23 percent in 1997.
"We think the letter tries to cool down the overheated stock market," said National Securities analyst Eric Liu.
The letter, also obtained by Reuters, urged brokers not to cooperate with underground securities organisations to manipulate share prices.
Lu said the recent market rallies reflected the recovering economy.

"The current heating market not only reflects the recovering economy, but also helps boost the efficiency of enterprises' fund raising to build up momentum for the national development," Lu said in the letter.
Lu also urged brokerages to offer investors convenient service in telephone consultation. --Taipei Newsroom (5080815)
